heading: What the model assumes
text: The protein unfolds in one step from the native state (N) to a final state (D), and the process cannot be reversed. Cooling the sample does not bring the protein back to the folded state, for example because it aggregates after unfolding. The unfolding is a first-order reaction whose rate depends on temperature according to the Arrhenius law (Sanchez-Ruiz model).

heading: Why the scan rate matters
text: The process is controlled by kinetics, not by an equilibrium. The faster the sample is heated, the higher the temperature at which the peak appears. The same protein therefore gives a different peak position at 0.5 K/min than at 1 K/min. The scan rate must be entered when fitting, and the peak temperature is not a true equilibrium melting temperature.

heading: T* (temperature of one unfolding per minute)
text: T* is the temperature at which the rate constant equals 1 per minute. It describes where the unfolding becomes fast for the given kinetics, and it does not depend on the scan rate.

heading: Ea (activation energy)
text: Ea is the energy barrier of the unfolding. It describes how strongly the unfolding rate increases with temperature. A larger Ea gives a sharper and narrower peak. In the app it is shown in kcal/mol.

heading: ΔH (unfolding enthalpy)
text: ΔH is the heat absorbed by the unfolding of one mole of protein, which is the area under the peak. For an irreversible process it is not an equilibrium value, so no Gibbs energy (ΔG) or stability curve can be derived from it.

heading: Baseline and fitting
text: A straight baseline is fitted together with the model. The app fits one scan rate at a time. Fitting several scan rates together gives a more precise Ea, but this global fit exists only in the backend and is not available in the web interface yet.

heading: What the app can do
text: ThermoFit fits differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) curves with two models: a reversible two-state model and an irreversible N → D model. It reports the fitted parameters with uncertainties and the quality of the fit (R² and the typical deviation).

heading: What the app cannot do
text:
- It fits only DSC data. Other methods such as fluorescence or circular dichroism are not supported.
- The two-state model assumes one cooperative transition with a constant ΔCp. Multi-domain proteins, intermediate states and aggregation need more elaborate models that are not implemented.
- The irreversible model describes a single N → D step. More complex mechanisms are not covered.
- The baseline is a straight line. A sigmoidal baseline is not available.
- The web interface fits one scan rate at a time.
- The app does not give medical, regulatory or GxP-validated results. It is a research and learning tool.

heading: How reliable the results are
text:
- Uncertainties come from a linear approximation, not from bootstrapping.
- On real curves, the residuals are structured near the peak, up to about 4 % of the peak height. The ideal model is a very good, but not a perfect description.
- On the digitized thesis curves, Tm agrees with the published values within about 0.1 °C. ΔH is about 2 % higher than published, and the reason is not established.

heading: About the demo data
text: The simulated demo curves are not measurements. The thesis demo curves are digitized from published figures (A. V. Kladova, Int. J. Biol. Macromol. 45:524, 2009), not raw instrument files.

heading: What the assistant does not know
text: The assistant explains the fit and the models using only this knowledge base. It cannot judge the quality of the sample, the experiment or the biological meaning of a result beyond what is described here.

heading: What the model assumes
text: The protein exists in only two states: folded (N) and unfolded (D). The two states convert into each other reversibly, so the unfolded protein can fold back when the sample is cooled. The unfolding is treated as one cooperative transition: the whole protein unfolds in a single step, with no stable intermediate states.

heading: What the plot shows
text: The x axis is the temperature in °C. The y axis is the excess heat capacity Cp, meaning the extra heat the sample absorbs per degree of heating. Unfolding absorbs heat, so the curve shows a peak. The fitted line is the model curve plus a straight baseline.

heading: Tm (melting temperature)
text: Tm is the temperature at which half of the protein is unfolded. It is also the position of the peak maximum. A higher Tm means the protein is more thermally stable.

heading: ΔH (unfolding enthalpy)
text: ΔH is the total heat absorbed when one mole of protein unfolds. It is the area under the peak, not the peak height. A larger ΔH means more heat is needed to unfold the protein. In the app it is shown in kcal/mol.

heading: ΔCp (heat-capacity change)
text: ΔCp is the difference in heat capacity between the unfolded and the folded state. It makes the heat capacity step up across the transition and determines how the stability changes with temperature. Fitting ΔCp together with a free baseline slope is poorly determined, so ΔCp is only fitted when the user switches "fit ΔCp" on.

heading: Baseline
text: The instrument background is described by a straight line (offset and slope) that is fitted together with the model. A sigmoidal (progress) baseline is not implemented.

heading: Uncertainties
text: The uncertainty (±) and the 95 % range of each parameter come from the least-squares covariance matrix. This is a linear approximation, not a bootstrap.
